chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Waddad, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I departed from Kufa on a ship to Qasr ibn Hubayra, which is about twenty farsakhs from Kufa across the water. I traveled that day shortening the prayer. Then it occurred to me at night to return to Kufa, so I did not know whether to shorten or complete the prayer upon my return, and what I should do.
He said: If you traveled on the day you departed at a steady pace (breid), then upon your return you must shorten the prayer, because you remained a traveler until you reached your home.

He said: And if you did not travel on the day you departed at a steady pace, then you must make up every prayer you shortened that day by praying it fully, before you stop at that place, because you did not reach the distance that permits shortening until you returned. Thus, it became obligatory upon you to make up what you shortened, and upon your return you must complete the prayer until you reach your home.

key_terms.التَّقْصِير: Shortening the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs during travel
key_terms.بَرِيداً: At a steady pace or distance, indicating valid travel status
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: Making up for missed or incorrectly performed prayers
key_terms.مُسَافِراً: A traveler, one eligible for shortening prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayer if a traveler turns back before reaching the minimum distance for qasr?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of *qasr* (shortening prayer) when a traveler reverses direction before completing the requisite distance (*qasr* threshold). Al-Tusi includes this to distinguish between a continuous journey where the traveler retains their status, versus a failed journey where the initial shortening was premature and requires *qada* (making up) by performing full prayers.
